links.outcome: Final-answer accuracy of rule-grounded tool-augmented LLM versus one-shot prompting and SFT-only baselines
links.effect: 86.73% final-answer accuracy, outperforming one-shot prompting by 24.0 and SFT-only by 17.27 percentage points; gains primarily driven by rule-grounded tool synthesis and schema-constrained extraction.
links.quote: Ablation and error analyses show that these performance gains are primarily driven by rule-grounded tool synthesis and schema-constrained extraction, whereas remaining failures are concentrated in clinical-semantic extraction and benchmark-specific output contracts.

links.outcome: Arithmetic and calculation errors by direct LLM prompting on medical calculators
links.effect: One-shot prompting was about 24.0 points below the tool-augmented method's 86.73% accuracy; remaining failures in clinical-semantic extraction and output contracts.
links.quote: By grounding calculator logic in executable tools, the proposed approach alleviates arithmetic hallucinations and improves the computational reliability of the final clinical outputs.

unlisted_practices: Using LLM-generated executable tools for deterministic medical calculation separated from clinical language extraction
Schema-constrained extraction of calculator inputs from patient notes

screen.reason: Evaluates tool augmentation and constrained extraction as a safeguard against arithmetic hallucinations compared to standard LLM prompting/fine-tuning on the MedCalc-Bench benchmark.
